title: CBSE Class 10 Science · Practice paper 2
subject: Science
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 39 questions. All questions are compulsory.

The question paper is divided into three sections:
Section A: Biology (30 marks), questions 1 to 16
Section B: Chemistry (25 marks), questions 17 to 29
Section C: Physics (25 marks), questions 30 to 39
Each section has multiple choice questions (MCQs), assertion-reason questions, short answer questions, a case-based question and a long answer question. Marks are given against each question.
Case-based questions carry 4 marks each and have three sub-parts.
Write the answers of each section in that section only. Do not mix the answers of one section with another.
Internal choices of the board paper are not included: each question has one version.
This is a practice paper written in the pattern of the CBSE Sample Question Paper 2026-27. It is not an official CBSE paper.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which option shows the correct sequence of steps in the nutrition of human beings?
questions.sol: Food is first taken in (ingestion), broken down (digestion), the digested food is absorbed into the blood (absorption), used by the cells (assimilation), and the undigested remains are removed (egestion).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters the human heart through the:
options: vena cava, into the right atrium
pulmonary artery, into the right ventricle
pulmonary vein, into the left atrium
questions.sol: The pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The vena cava brings deoxygenated blood to the right atrium.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A blood test shows that a patient has a very high level of urea in the blood. Which organ is most likely not working properly?
questions.sol: Urea is removed from the blood by filtration in the kidneys. If the kidneys do not work properly, urea builds up in the blood.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A person has a swollen neck. The doctor advises the person to use iodised salt. Which gland is affected and which hormone does it make?
questions.sol: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxine. Lack of iodine causes goitre, a swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A tall pea plant (Tt) is crossed with a dwarf pea plant (tt). What fraction of the offspring is expected to be dwarf?
questions.sol: Tt gives T and t gametes in equal numbers; tt gives only t. Offspring: Tt (tall) and tt (dwarf) in the ratio 1 : 1, so half are dwarf.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a human-made ecosystem?
questions.sol: Crop fields and gardens are ecosystems created and maintained by human beings. Forests, ponds and lakes are natural ecosystems.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If all the decomposers in an ecosystem disappeared, what would happen?
options: Producers would get more nutrients from the soil.
Energy would flow faster to the top consumers.
The number of herbivores would increase at once.
Dead remains would pile up and nutrients would not be returned to the soil.
questions.sol: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals and return the nutrients to the soil. Without them, dead remains would collect and nutrients would not be recycled for producers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The following question consists of two statements: Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer it by selecting the appropriate option.
Assertion (A): Water and minerals absorbed by the roots reach the leaves through the xylem.
Reason (R): Food made in the leaves is carried to other parts of the plant through the phloem.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol: Both statements are true, but R is about the transport of food in the phloem. It does not explain how water and minerals move up through the xylem.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The following question consists of two statements: Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer it by selecting the appropriate option.
Assertion (A): Green plants in an ecosystem are called producers.
Reason (R): Green plants capture about 10% of the solar energy that falls on their leaves.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol: Green plants are producers because they make food from sunlight, so A is true. They capture only about 1% of the solar energy falling on the leaves, so R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Glucose is broken down in the absence of oxygen in yeast and also in human muscle cells during heavy exercise.
(a) Name the end products of this breakdown in each case.
(b) In which part of the cell does the first step, the breakdown of glucose into pyruvate, take place?
questions.model:
(a) In yeast: ethanol and carbon dioxide (with release of energy). In human muscle cells: lactic acid (with release of energy).
(b) In the cytoplasm.

points.t: Yeast: ethanol
Yeast: carbon dioxide
Muscle cells: lactic acid
Cytoplasm

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) How is ozone formed in the upper atmosphere?
(b) Why is the depletion of the ozone layer a cause of concern?
questions.model:
(a) High-energy ultraviolet radiation splits some oxygen molecules ($\mathrm{O_2}$) into free oxygen atoms ($\mathrm{O}$). These atoms combine with oxygen molecules to form ozone: $\mathrm{O_2 \rightarrow O + O}$; $\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}$.
(b) The ozone layer shields the surface of the Earth from the harmful ultraviolet radiation of the Sun. If it becomes thinner, more ultraviolet radiation reaches the Earth, which can cause skin cancer in human beings and harm other organisms.

points.t: UV radiation splits $\mathrm{O_2}$ into oxygen atoms
Oxygen atoms combine with $\mathrm{O_2}$ to form $\mathrm{O_3}$
Ozone layer shields the Earth from harmful UV radiation; depletion lets more UV in, causing harm such as skin cancer

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: State two features of the small intestine that help it absorb digested food efficiently. Give the role of each feature.
questions.model:
1. The inner lining of the small intestine has numerous finger-like projections called villi. They greatly increase the surface area for absorption.
2. The villi are richly supplied with blood vessels, which take the absorbed food to every cell of the body.
(The great length of the small intestine, which gives food more time and area for absorption, is also accepted.)

points.t: Villi increase the surface area for absorption
Villi have a rich supply of blood vessels that carry absorbed food away (or great length of intestine)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Write the balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis.
(b) Desert plants keep their stomata closed during the day. How do they still carry out photosynthesis?
(c) A potted plant is kept in a dark room for two days, and then a leaf is tested with iodine solution. The leaf does not turn blue-black. Explain why.
questions.model:
(a) $\mathrm{6CO_2 + 12H_2O \xrightarrow[\text{chlorophyll}]{\text{sunlight}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 + 6H_2O}$
(b) Desert plants open their stomata at night and take in carbon dioxide, which is stored in the form of an intermediate (an acid). During the day, when the leaves absorb light energy, this stored carbon dioxide is used to make food.
(c) In the dark, no photosynthesis takes place, so no new starch is made. The starch already present in the leaf is used up during the two days, so the leaf gives a negative starch test.

points.t: Balanced equation with sunlight and chlorophyll
$\mathrm{CO_2}$ taken in at night and stored as an intermediate, used during the day
No photosynthesis in the dark and stored starch is used up, so no starch is present

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Explain how the sex of a child is determined in human beings.
(b) A family blames the mother for giving birth only to daughters. Is this correct? Justify your answer.
questions.model:
(a) A woman has a perfect pair of sex chromosomes, XX, so all her eggs carry an X chromosome. A man has a mismatched pair, XY, so half of his sperms carry an X chromosome and half carry a Y chromosome. If a sperm carrying X fertilises the egg, the child is XX, a girl. If a sperm carrying Y fertilises the egg, the child is XY, a boy.
(b) No, it is not correct. The mother contributes only an X chromosome. The sex of the child depends on whether the sperm from the father carries an X or a Y chromosome.

points.t: Female XX: all eggs carry X
Male XY: sperms carry X or Y (half each)
X sperm + egg gives XX (girl)
Y sperm + egg gives XY (boy)
Not correct: mother gives only X; sex depends on X or Y from the father's sperm

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Arjun is the opening batsman of his school cricket team. Just before the final match, he feels nervous: his heart beats fast and he breathes quickly. During his innings he has to watch a fast-moving ball, move his bat at the right moment and keep his balance while running between the wickets. Messages travel rapidly through his nervous system from his eyes to his brain and from his brain to his muscles.

parts.q: (i) Name the hormone that is released when Arjun feels nervous, and the gland that secretes it.
parts.model: Adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands.

points.t: Adrenaline
Adrenal gland

parts.q: (ii) State one effect of this hormone that prepares the body to deal with the situation.
parts.model: Any one: the heart beats faster, so more oxygen is supplied to the muscles; blood supply to the digestive system and skin is reduced and diverted to the skeletal muscles; the breathing rate increases.

points.t: Any one correct effect (faster heartbeat supplying more oxygen to muscles, blood diverted to skeletal muscles, or faster breathing)

parts.q:
(iii) (a) Name the part of the brain that maintains posture and balance of the body.
(b) How is a message passed from one neuron to the next neuron?
parts.model:
(a) Cerebellum (part of the hind-brain).
(b) The electrical impulse reaches the end of the axon of the first neuron and causes the release of chemicals. These chemicals cross the small gap (synapse) and start a similar electrical impulse in the dendrite of the next neuron.

points.t: Cerebellum
Impulse at axon end releases chemicals that cross the synapse and start an impulse in the next neuron's dendrite

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Distinguish between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
(b) Describe the events that take place after a pollen grain lands on a suitable stigma, up to the formation of the zygote.
(c) After fertilisation, what does each of the following develop into: (i) zygote, (ii) ovule, (iii) ovary? What happens to the petals and sepals?
questions.model:
(a) Self-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower (or another flower of the same plant). Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of a flower of one plant to the stigma of a flower of another plant of the same kind.
(b) The pollen grain on the stigma grows a pollen tube, which travels down through the style and reaches the ovule in the ovary. The male germ cell moves through the tube and fuses with the female germ cell (egg) in the ovule. This fusion forms the zygote.
(c) (i) The zygote divides several times to form the embryo. (ii) The ovule develops a tough coat and becomes the seed. (iii) The ovary grows rapidly and ripens to form the fruit. The petals and sepals (with the stamens, style and stigma) shrivel and fall off.

points.t: Self-pollination: pollen to stigma of same flower/plant
Cross-pollination: pollen to stigma of a flower on another plant
Pollen tube grows from the pollen grain through the style to the ovule
Male germ cell fuses with the egg in the ovule, forming the zygote
(i) Zygote: embryo
(ii) Ovule: seed
(iii) Ovary: fruit
Petals and sepals shrivel and fall off

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: When solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate are mixed, a white precipitate is formed. Which option correctly names the precipitate and the type of reaction?
questions.sol: $\mathrm{BaCl_2 + Na_2SO_4 \rightarrow BaSO_4 + 2NaCl}$. The ions are exchanged (double displacement) and insoluble white barium sulphate precipitates; sodium chloride stays in solution.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A few drops of phenolphthalein are added to each of the following. Which one turns pink?
questions.sol: Phenolphthalein turns pink only in a basic solution. Lime water (calcium hydroxide solution) is basic; vinegar, lemon juice and soda water are acidic.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Plaster of Paris should be stored in a moisture-proof container because it:
options: reacts with water and sets into a hard mass of gypsum
absorbs carbon dioxide and becomes washing soda
questions.sol: Plaster of Paris ($\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O}$) combines with water to form gypsum ($\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}$), a hard solid, so moisture would spoil it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In which of the following will a displacement reaction NOT take place?
options: Zinc granules added to copper sulphate solution
Iron nail dipped in copper sulphate solution
Copper wire dipped in iron sulphate solution
Magnesium ribbon dipped in zinc sulphate solution
questions.sol: A metal displaces only a less reactive metal from its salt solution. Copper is less reactive than iron, so it cannot displace iron from iron sulphate.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of ethane ($\mathrm{C_2H_6}$)?
questions.sol: Ethane has one C-C single bond and six C-H single bonds: 1 + 6 = 7 covalent bonds.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Thin foils of silver used to decorate sweets are made by hammering silver. Which property of metals does this use?
questions.sol: Malleability is the property of being beaten into thin sheets. Ductility is the property of being drawn into wires.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which of the following pairs of compounds belongs to the same homologous series?
questions.sol: $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$ and $\mathrm{C_3H_8}$ are both alkanes ($\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$) and differ by one $\mathrm{CH_2}$ unit. The other pairs mix alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The following question consists of two statements: Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer it by selecting the appropriate option.
Assertion (A): While diluting a concentrated acid, the acid should be added slowly to water and not water to the acid.
Reason (R): Mixing a concentrated acid with water is a highly exothermic process.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol: Both statements are true. Because a lot of heat is released, adding water to the acid can make the mixture splash out and cause burns; adding acid slowly to a large amount of water keeps it safe. So R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Draw the electron dot structures of (i) a nitrogen molecule, $\mathrm{N_2}$, and (ii) an ethene molecule, $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$. Show all the valence electrons. (Atomic numbers: N = 7, C = 6, H = 1)
questions.model:
The diagrams must show the following.
(i) Each nitrogen atom has 5 valence electrons. The two nitrogen atoms share three pairs of electrons, so there is a triple bond, N$\equiv$N. Each nitrogen atom also has one unshared (lone) pair of electrons, which completes its octet.
(ii) In ethene, the two carbon atoms share two pairs of electrons (a double bond, C=C). Each carbon atom shares one pair of electrons with each of two hydrogen atoms, so every carbon has an octet and every hydrogen has a duplet.

points.t: $\mathrm{N_2}$: three shared pairs of electrons between the two N atoms (triple bond)
$\mathrm{N_2}$: one unshared (lone) pair on each N atom, so each N has 8 electrons
Ethene: two shared pairs of electrons between the two C atoms (double bond)
Ethene: each C shares one pair with each of two H atoms (12 valence electrons shown in all)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Write the chemical equation for the preparation of bleaching powder from dry slaked lime, and give one use of bleaching powder.
(b) Write the chemical formula of washing soda and give one use of it.
(c) Name the gas produced at the anode during the electrolysis of brine (chlor-alkali process).
questions.model:
(a) $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CaOCl_2 + H_2O}$
Use (any one): bleaching cotton and linen in the textile industry or wood pulp in paper factories; disinfecting drinking water; as an oxidising agent in industry.
(b) $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}$. Use (any one): in the glass, soap and paper industries; for removing permanent hardness of water; as a cleaning agent at home; to make borax.
(c) Chlorine.

points.t: Correct equation: $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CaOCl_2 + H_2O}$
One correct use of bleaching powder
Formula $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}$
One correct use of washing soda
Chlorine

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) A cook notices that the bottoms of the cooking vessels are getting blackened on the gas stove. What does this show, and what should be done?
(b) What is formed when ethanol is heated with alkaline potassium permanganate solution? What is the role of the potassium permanganate?
(c) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of methane with chlorine in the presence of sunlight, and name the type of reaction.
questions.model:
(a) It shows incomplete combustion of the fuel, because the supply of air is not enough (the flame is yellow and sooty). The air holes of the burner should be cleaned (opened) so that more air enters.
(b) Ethanoic acid is formed. Alkaline potassium permanganate acts as an oxidising agent (it adds oxygen to ethanol).
(c) $\mathrm{CH_4 + Cl_2 \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} CH_3Cl + HCl}$. It is a substitution reaction.

points.t: Incomplete combustion due to insufficient air
Clean the air holes of the burner to let in more air
Ethanoic acid is formed
Potassium permanganate is an oxidising agent
Equation $\mathrm{CH_4 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CH_3Cl + HCl}$
Substitution reaction

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
To study rusting, a student set up four test tubes, each containing a clean iron nail:
Tube A: nail in ordinary tap water, open to the air.
Tube B: nail in boiled distilled water, with a layer of oil on top of the water.
Tube C: nail in dry air, with some anhydrous calcium chloride in the tube.
Tube D: galvanised iron nail in ordinary tap water, open to the air.
The tubes were left for one week.

parts.q: (i) In which test tube will the nail rust?
parts.model: Tube A, because there the nail is in contact with both air (oxygen) and water.

points.t: Tube A

parts.q: (ii) Why is a layer of oil put on the water in tube B, and why is anhydrous calcium chloride kept in tube C?
parts.model: The oil layer stops air from dissolving again in the boiled water. Anhydrous calcium chloride absorbs moisture and keeps the air in tube C dry.

points.t: Oil stops air from dissolving in the water
Calcium chloride absorbs moisture (keeps air dry)

parts.q:
(iii) (a) Why does a galvanised nail not rust even if its zinc coating gets scratched?
(b) Stainless steel is an alloy that does not rust. Name the two metals mixed with iron to make it.
parts.model:
(a) Zinc is more reactive than iron. Even when the coating is broken, zinc reacts with air and moisture in preference to iron, so the iron stays protected.
(b) Nickel and chromium.

points.t: Zinc is more reactive than iron and corrodes in preference, protecting the iron
Nickel
Chromium

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) A student heats a few crystals of ferrous sulphate in a dry boiling tube.
(i) What colour change is seen in the solid?
(ii) What smell is noticed?
(iii) Write the balanced chemical equation and name the type of reaction.
(b) Silver chloride is stored in dark-coloured bottles. Explain why, with a chemical equation.
(c) Chips and other foods containing oils are often packed in bags filled with nitrogen. Explain why.
questions.model:
(a) (i) The green crystals first lose water and then change into a reddish-brown solid (ferric oxide).
(ii) A smell of burning sulphur (due to sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide gases).
(iii) $\mathrm{2FeSO_4 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Fe_2O_3 + SO_2 + SO_3}$. It is a (thermal) decomposition reaction.
(b) In sunlight, silver chloride decomposes into silver and chlorine: $\mathrm{2AgCl \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag + Cl_2}$. Dark bottles keep out light and prevent this decomposition.
(c) Oils and fats get oxidised by air and become rancid, changing their smell and taste. Nitrogen does not react with the food and keeps oxygen away, so it prevents oxidation (rancidity).

points.t: Green colour changes to reddish-brown
Smell of burning sulphur
Balanced equation $\mathrm{2FeSO_4 \rightarrow Fe_2O_3 + SO_2 + SO_3}$
(Thermal) decomposition reaction
Equation $\mathrm{2AgCl \rightarrow 2Ag + Cl_2}$ in sunlight
Dark bottles keep out light and prevent decomposition
Oils get oxidised by air and become rancid
Nitrogen keeps oxygen away, preventing oxidation

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A student sitting in the last row of the classroom cannot read the writing on the board clearly, but can read her book easily. Which option gives her defect of vision and the lens that will correct it?
questions.sol: She cannot see distant objects clearly but sees nearby objects well, so she has myopia (near-sightedness). It is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A wire of length $l$ and area of cross-section $A$ has resistance $R$. What is the resistance of another wire of the same material with length $2l$ and area of cross-section $2A$?
questions.sol: $R = \rho l / A$. For the new wire, $R' = \rho (2l)/(2A) = \rho l/A = R$.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The following question consists of two statements: Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer it by selecting the appropriate option.
Assertion (A): The focal length of a concave mirror whose radius of curvature is 30 cm is 60 cm.
Reason (R): For spherical mirrors of small aperture, the radius of curvature is equal to twice the focal length.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol: Since $R = 2f$, the focal length is $f = R/2 = 30/2 = 15$ cm, not 60 cm. So A is false and R is true.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: White light is passed through a glass prism and, separately, through a rectangular glass slab. A spectrum is seen with the prism but not with the slab. Explain why.
questions.model:
In a glass prism, the two refracting surfaces are inclined to each other. The different colours bend through different angles, and at the second surface they bend further apart, so they spread out and form a spectrum.
In a rectangular glass slab, the two refracting surfaces are parallel. The bending at the second surface is equal and opposite to that at the first, so all the colours come out parallel to the incident ray and overlap again. Hence no spectrum is seen.

points.t: Prism: inclined surfaces; colours deviate through different angles and spread out
Slab: parallel surfaces; emergent colours are parallel to the incident ray and overlap, so no spectrum

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An electric heater of resistance 20 $\Omega$ draws a current of 5 A from the mains. Calculate the heat produced by it in 1 minute.
questions.model:
By Joule's law of heating, $H = I^2 R t$.
$H = 5^2 \times 20 \times 60 = 25 \times 20 \times 60 = 30000$ J $= 3 \times 10^4$ J.

points.t: Uses $H = I^2 R t$ with $t = 60$ s

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) How do the ciliary muscles help the eye to see a nearby object clearly?
(b) What is presbyopia? Why does it occur?
(c) A person with presbyopia uses bifocal lenses. Which type of lens forms the upper part of a bifocal lens and which forms the lower part?
questions.model:
(a) To see a nearby object, the ciliary muscles contract. The eye lens becomes thicker, its focal length decreases, and the image of the nearby object is focused on the retina.
(b) Presbyopia is the defect in which the power of accommodation of the eye decreases with age, so the near point moves farther away and nearby objects are not seen clearly. It occurs because the ciliary muscles weaken and the eye lens becomes less flexible.
(c) The upper part is a concave lens (for distant vision); the lower part is a convex lens (for near vision).

points.t: Ciliary muscles contract, lens becomes thicker and its focal length decreases
Presbyopia: power of accommodation decreases with age (near point recedes)
Cause: weakening of ciliary muscles and reduced flexibility of the eye lens
Upper part concave (distant vision)
Lower part convex (near vision)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Describe the pattern of the magnetic field lines (i) around a straight wire carrying current, and (ii) inside a long solenoid carrying current.
(b) A vertical wire carries current upwards. Seen from above, what is the direction of the magnetic field lines around it?
(c) Which material is used for the core of an electromagnet? Give one reason.
questions.model:
(a) (i) The field lines are concentric circles around the wire, with the wire at the centre, in a plane perpendicular to the wire.
(ii) Inside a long solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines, showing that the field is the same at all points inside (uniform).
(b) By the right-hand thumb rule (thumb pointing upwards along the current), the fingers curl anticlockwise when seen from above. The field lines are anticlockwise.
(c) Soft iron. It becomes a strong magnet when current flows in the coil and loses its magnetism as soon as the current is switched off.

points.t: (i) Concentric circles around the wire
(ii) Parallel straight lines inside the solenoid (uniform field)
Anticlockwise (seen from above)
Soft iron
Reason: magnetised strongly when current flows and loses magnetism when current stops

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Two resistors of 10 $\Omega$ and 15 $\Omega$ are available.
(a) Find the current drawn when they are connected in series to a 10 V supply.
(b) Find the total current drawn when they are connected in parallel to a 6 V supply.
(c) Give two reasons why electrical appliances in homes are connected in parallel and not in series.
questions.model:
(a) Series: $R = 10 + 15 = 25\ \Omega$; $I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{10}{25} = 0.4$ A.
(b) Parallel: $\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 + 2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{6}$, so $R_p = 6\ \Omega$; $I = \dfrac{6}{6} = 1$ A.
(c) Any two: each appliance gets the full mains voltage; if one appliance fails or is switched off, the others keep working; each appliance can be switched on or off separately; each appliance draws the current it needs according to its own resistance.

points.t: Series: $R = 25\ \Omega$ and $I = 0.4$ A
Parallel: $R_p = 6\ \Omega$ and $I = 1$ A
First correct reason (for example, each appliance gets full voltage)
Second correct reason (for example, one failing does not stop the others)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Ravi's house has a domestic circuit with three wires: a live wire with red insulation, a neutral wire with black insulation and an earth wire with green insulation. The kitchen circuit is protected by a 10 A fuse. One morning, Ravi switches on an electric kettle of 2200 W and a toaster of 1100 W together on the kitchen circuit. Later in the day, an electrician warns him that some old wiring in the kitchen is loose and could cause a short circuit.

parts.q: (i) What is the potential difference between the live wire and the neutral wire in Indian homes?
(ii) Will the 10 A fuse blow when the kettle and the toaster are used together? Show your working.
parts.model: Total power = 2200 + 1100 = 3300 W. Current $I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{3300}{220} = 15$ A. This is more than 10 A, so the fuse will blow (melt).

points.t: Yes, the fuse blows since 15 A is more than 10 A

parts.q:
(iii) (a) Why is the metal body of the kettle connected to the earth wire?
(b) What is meant by a short circuit? What happens to the current in the circuit when it occurs?
parts.model:
(a) The earth wire provides a low-resistance path for current. If the live wire touches the metal body due to a fault, the current leaks to the earth and the user does not get a severe electric shock.
(b) A short circuit occurs when the live wire and the neutral wire come into direct contact. The resistance of the circuit becomes very small, so the current in the circuit increases suddenly to a very large value.

points.t: Earth wire gives a low-resistance path for leakage current, so the user does not get a shock
Short circuit: live and neutral wires touch directly
Resistance becomes very small and current increases sharply

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Define the power of a lens and give its SI unit.
(b) An object 3 cm high is placed 15 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the position, size and nature of the image.
(c) A concave lens has a power of $-2.5$ D. Find its focal length.
questions.model:
(a) The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length (in metres): $P = \dfrac{1}{f}$. It shows the degree to which the lens converges or diverges light. SI unit: dioptre (D).
(b) $u = -15$ cm, $f = +10$ cm.
Lens formula: $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$, so $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$
$v = +30$ cm: the image is 30 cm from the lens on the other side.
Magnification $m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{30}{-15} = -2$
Height of image $h' = m \times h = -2 \times 3 = -6$ cm.
The image is real, inverted and magnified (6 cm tall).
(c) $f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{-2.5}$ m $= -0.4$ m $= -40$ cm.
